title: Microsoft Teams: attendee chat in town halls for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold: the government-cloud default is presented as user opt-in even though the cited documentation excludes those clouds and the roadmap does not state their default. Microsoft also publishes attendee-chat licensing and capacity requirements that the briefing reports as unpublished. The control paths, commands and commercial-service limitations are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans public event chat for all users in events larger than 1,000 users or any event optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: All users in Events larger than 1,000 users or in any Event optimized for a large audience can now chat with one another in a public event chat in GCC, GCC High and DoD.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Meeting chat meeting policy governs meetings and events up to 1,000 attendees rather than large-audience attendee chat.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control: Whether participants in your users' meetings and events with up to 1,000 attendees can read and send chat messages.

claims.claim: The Meeting chat meeting policy includes options that exclude anonymous users.
claims.quote: On for everyone but anonymous users | EnabledExceptAnonymous | All participants, except anonymous ones, can read and send chat messages.

claims.claim: The events policy is user-level.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Use this cmdlet to update an existing policy.

claims.claim: The events-policy chat control decides whether the organizer may enable chat, rather than selecting individual attendees who may type.
claims.quote: This setting governs whether the user can enable the Comment Stream chat experience for an event optimized for a large audience.

claims.claim: Turning off Events optimized for a large audience after scheduling prevents the organizer from running or starting the event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference describes the policy as currently still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The chat control is in Teams admin center at Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience chat experience.
claims.quote: Go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select the policy you want to edit or create a new one. ... In the Events optimized for a large audience chat experience dropdown list, select Optimized (the default value) or None.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None turns off attendee chat for organizers under that policy.
claims.quote: To turn off chat for attendees in events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None

claims.claim: The attendance control is in Teams admin center at Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: Go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following:

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests restricts attendance to the organization and guests.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.claim: The town-hall creation control is in Teams admin center at Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: Go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organizers under that policy from creating large-audience events.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The documented events attendance policy defaults to Everyone, permitting users outside the organization to attend.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone. When users with this policy create events with up to 1,000 attendees or events optimized for large audiences, any user can attend.

claims.claim: The documented attendance-policy values are Everyone, EveryoneInOrganization and EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests.
claims.quote: -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess(Everyone,EveryoneInOrganization,EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests)

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Teams service description lists Town halls (Teams events) as available in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: | Feature | Teams Business plans | Teams Enterprise plans | GCC | GCC - High | DOD | Education | ... | Town halls (Teams events) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature comparison lists Comment stream for large-audience events without a Premium marking.
claims.quote: | Chat | [checkmark] | [checkmark] | Comment stream^2^ | ... ^2^ Available in events with up to 20,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Attendee chat is included without stating which license covers the large-audience experience or its licensed capacity.
claims.quote: To host events with more than 3,000 attendees with engagement capabilities (chat, reactions, raise hand, polls, Q&A), organizations must purchase Attendee Capacity Pack add-on licenses and assign them to organizers.
claims.fix: Keep included for the chat capability itself, but replace licensing.notes with: 'Attendee chat is included in eligible Teams event licenses. Teams Enterprise supports interactive events with up to 3,000 attendees; larger interactive events require an appropriately sized Attendee Capacity Pack assigned to the organizer, except while an eligible pre-April 1, 2026 Teams Premium term remains active. Packs are available in GCC, GCC High and DoD. Chat remains limited to events with up to 20,000 attendees.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-add-on-licensing/attendee-capacity-pack alongside the existing chat reference.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the license covering event chat.
claims.quote: Chat for attendees | Organizers can allow attendees to use chat during events. | Manage chat for Teams events
claims.fix: Replace the licensing-absence statement with: 'Microsoft publishes attendee-chat entitlement in its Teams events licensing overview; chat is listed under both foundational and advanced event features, with capacity depending on the organizer's license.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing. Retain only the narrower absence that no separate per-chat price is published, and include the capacity qualification specified for licensing.notes.

claims.claim: The cited service description and feature comparison publish no separate event-chat meter or per-chat price.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams town hall attendee comment stream chat licensing price meter; Teams event attendee chat automated actions bots public comment stream licensing meter price. Read service description, feature comparison, events licensing and eCDN purchasing; no separate per-chat meter or price found.

claims.claim: The planned government-cloud feature arrives in a user-opt-in state.
claims.quote: Searched: "573625" "chat" default GCC; "TownhallChatExperience" "GCC" default. Read roadmap, manage-event-chat and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy. The roadmap states no government default; Learn still excludes GCC, GCCH and DoD.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Add: 'Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for the government-cloud release. The commercial documentation allows organizers to enable attendee chat under the default Optimized policy.' Keep the government-default open question and the conditional wording in Why it matters.

claims.claim: The roadmap and chat documentation describe human chat, not new automated actions.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams event attendee chat automated actions bots public comment stream licensing meter price. Read roadmap and manage-event-chat: users chat with one another and organizers enable attendee messages; neither describes new automated actions.

claims.claim: A content search for the organizer can find attendee chat messages in the documented storage period.
claims.quote: During this time, if you do a content search for the organizer, you can see all the messages that were sent in that chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview can be used to place an organizer's Exchange mailbox on a hold.
claims.quote: Place a hold on the Exchange mailboxes ... Go to the Microsoft Purview portal ... Select the eDiscovery solution card and then select Cases ... Select a case, and then select the Hold policies tab.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-hold-create for the Purview statement and narrow it to 'An eDiscovery hold on the organizer's Exchange mailbox can be created in Microsoft Purview.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist includes mailbox holds and content search, but neither control appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Agree how a hold is requested for events that need longer. ... Run a content search of an organiser's mailbox ... [The controls table contains only chat experience, attendance and event creation.]
claims.fix: Remove the checklist clause 'and agree how a hold is requested for events that need longer' and the After rollout content-search bullet. Keep the sourced explanation of storage and holds in the prose; do not add unverified control rows.
